Nicholas “The Reaper” Irving and former SEAL Team Six operator Robert O’Neill join VladTV for a candid breakdown of how elite U.S. special operations units differ in training, mission roles, and battlefield execution. O’Neill explains the pipeline from Navy SEALs to DEVGRU, the experience level at Delta Force, and how Army Rangers, RRC, Task Force 160, and tier-one teams worked together in Afghanistan. recentItems.title: Clavicular, Who is Currently Charged with R***, Tells His Life Story (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit when Clavicular sat down with VladTV.

Braden Eric Peters, better known online as Clavicular, sat down with VladTV to discuss his rise as one of the internet’s most controversial looksmaxing influencers. Originally from Hoboken, New Jersey, Clavicular explained how he became obsessed with physical optimization at a young age, eventually experimenting with testosterone at just 14 years old despite the legal and health risks involved.

The conversation delved into the world of looksmaxing, including facial aesthetics, physique enhancement, and controversial techniques aimed at improving appearance. Clavicular broke down concepts such as facial harmony and the Harmony Score, explaining how symmetry, proportions, and facial structure can influence perceived attractiveness. He also critiqued popular internet trends like thumb pulling and other methods he considered ineffective or misleading.

Clavicular discussed documenting his journey online, including his use of fat dissolvers, aromatase inhibitors for height optimization, and other unconventional approaches. He also addressed his eventual removal from YouTube for violating the platform’s community guidelines. Despite the controversy surrounding some of his methods, he argued that society already accepts cosmetic enhancement, particularly for women, while men pursuing similar changes can face ridicule.

The interview also explored the viral PSL attractiveness scale, ranging from “subhuman” to “god tier,” as well as broader debates surrounding beauty standards, confidence, status, and wealth in modern dating culture. Vlad challenged Clavicular on the importance of long-term thinking and sustainability, encouraging him to balance short-term internet attention with strategic planning for the future.

Throughout the conversation, Clavicular reflected on criticism, internet fame, and why he believes young men are increasingly drawn to self-improvement culture in search of confidence, validation, and success.

recentItems.title: Aries Spears' 1st VladTV Interview (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit Aries Spears’ first appearance on VladTV in 2016.

During the interview, the comedian touched on a wide range of topics. He began by discussing Dave Chappelle and claimed that Chappelle did not have a significant Black fanbase until the success of “Chappelle’s Show.” Spears also reflected on the nation’s mixed reaction to the O.J. Simpson verdict.

He went on to address Stacey Dash’s comments and actions before offering his thoughts on Kevin Hart. Spears also discussed rumors surrounding Paul Mooney, race relations in America, and the appeal of “Key & Peele” within the Black community.

recentItems.title: Royce White & Vlad on Their Past Internet Beef (Part 1)
recentItems.description:

--------
Former Houston Rockets player Royce White sits down with DJ Vlad for his first VladTV interview, opening with a candid look back at their 2022 online feud sparked by Vlad’s viral tweet about video games and depression. White says he doesn’t remember the exchange in detail, downplays the “beef,” and praises VladTV’s cultural impact and long-form interviews.

The conversation then shifts to White’s journey from Saint Paul and Minneapolis in the Twin Cities to becoming one of Minnesota’s top high school basketball stars. He reflects on being named Minnesota Mr. Basketball, winning two state championships, playing for DeLaSalle and Hopkins, and coming through the Howard Pulley Nike Elite program. White also discusses being a Jordan All-American, missing the McDonald’s All-American Game, Midwest recruiting politics, and how that fueled his college basketball ambitions. The interview also touches on his Senate runs, presidential aspirations, and public persona.
